VeilType works offline. Accessibility access observes keyboard window bounds and the foreground app for your rules. It never reads screen or typed text. Preferences, app rules and your chosen photo reference stay on this device. A veil is a visual aid, not protection against screenshots or cameras.

VeilType provides an optional privacy veil over other apps. When you enable its Android accessibility service, it observes top-level keyboard window type and bounds and the foreground app’s package name. It uses this information on your device to position the veil and apply app rules. VeilType does not traverse accessibility nodes or read text displayed or typed in other apps.

VeilType stores your settings, including app rules, schedules, appearance and control position, on your device. If you choose a photo, it stores a reference and uses Android document access to display the photo. The original stays with its document provider. Android may retain document access grants until revoked or the app is uninstalled.

VeilType has no internet permission and does not include accounts, advertising or analytics. It does not send this information to the developer.

Accessibility and display-over-other-apps access require your action in Android settings. VeilType uses them to detect the keyboard and draw the veil. You can disarm VeilType or revoke access in Android settings. Notification access controls visibility of service controls, subject to Android’s behavior. Optional boot access can restore the armed service if you enable it.

Preferences and app rules remain on your device until changed, the app’s data is cleared, or the app is uninstalled. Uninstalling removes local app data and Android document grants; it does not delete the original photo. A veil is a visual privacy aid and does not prevent screenshots, screen readers or cameras from capturing content.
For questions about VeilType and this policy, contact support.fintrace@gmail.com. The developer may update this policy when the app or its data practices change.

VeilType observes top-level window types and bounds to find the keyboard, and the foreground app name to apply your app rules. A separate display-over-apps permission lets it draw the veil.

VeilType does not read screen content, typed text, passwords, clipboard data or screenshots. Your settings, app rules and selected photo reference stay on this device. VeilType has no internet permission.
Android will show a broad warning because accessibility access is powerful. You can revoke it in Settings at any time.
